## Git workflow strategy

We used a branch-based Git workflow to work collaboratively and avoid conflicts. The `main` branch contains the final version of the project. Each question was developed in a separate branch, such as `question-1`, `question-2` and `question-3`.

Each team member works on the branch corresponding to their question and modifies only the relevant file in the `questions` folder. Werner did the first part, Shakir did the second part and Charles did the third part. Once the work is completed, the changes are committed with a meaningful commit message and pushed to GitHub. The branch can then be merged into `main`.

This workflow allows several team members to work simultaneously while reducing the risk of conflicts in the main document.

## Challenges encountered and lessons learned

During the project, we encountered several challenges related to Git, GitHub, RStudio and Quarto. In particular, we had to learn how to create and manage branches, commit changes, publish branches and organize the project into separate files.

We also learned that having a clear Git workflow is important when several people are working on the same project. Separating the questions into different files and branches makes collaboration easier and helps avoid merge conflicts.

Another challenge was understanding how Quarto documents are organized and how the different question files can be included in the main report. This helped us better understand the connection between the source `.qmd` files and the final PDF report.
